name: Pacific Blue
lede: Pacific Blue is a bright, slightly green-leaning sky blue named for the ocean, not for any dye or standard.

sections.title: An ocean's name
sections.body:
Pacific Blue takes its name directly from the Pacific Ocean, the way color lists also carry [[carolina-blue]] and [[columbia-blue]] for places rather than materials [1]. Our library records it only from Wikipedia, with no dictionary, standard or dye house behind it, so there is no coiner or date to give beyond that web record [1]. The name belongs to a wide family of ocean- and sky-named blues used in branding and everyday speech more than in historical color science [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[maximum-blue]], only 2.8 units off on screen, close enough to read as the same blue [2]; [[cyan-blue]] and [[cyan-blue]] both sit 4.0 units away [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within range of this swatch in just 1 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, which is rarer than 86 percent of the named colors in our library [3]. A bright, saturated cyan-blue like this is a modern dye and pigment range; it simply has little precedent in the mostly older paintings our archive holds [3]. This is a photograph of a varnished canvas read as a screen color, not a pigment identification, and here the sample is too thin to support any further claim [3].
